english.title: Temporarily released prisoner failed to comply with recall
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) having been temporarily released from

(A)_[His Majesty's prison]_
(B)_[His Majesty's remand centre]_
(C)_[His Majesty's young offenders institution]_

at **(..SPECIFY LOCATION OR ESTABLISHMENT..), knowing or believing an order recalling you had been made and while unlawfully at large by virtue of that order, failed, without reasonable excuse, to take all necessary steps for complying as soon as reasonably practicable with the order
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1) and (3) of the Prisoners (Return to Custody) Act 1995.
english.pointstoprove:

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The offence does not apply to person released from secure training centre (section 1(2)).
(ii) See also offence wording H12577.
(iii) Paragraph 17(1) of Schedule 1 to the Crime (Sentences) Act 1997 extends to the whole of the United Kingdom and Channel Islands the power to arrest and return prisoners unlawfully at large.
(iv) Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the offences to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.

other.powersofarrest:
Arrest without warrant
Any person who, having been sentenced to imprisonment, custody for life or youth custody or ordered to be detained in a detention centre or young offenders institution or a secure training centre, or having been committed to a prison or remand centre, is unlawfully at large, may be arrested by a constable without warrant and taken to the place in which he is required in accordance with law to be detained. (Section 49 Prisons Act 1952).
other.penalty:
Either way -
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2002; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 1(3)(b) of the Prisoners (Return to Custody) Act 1995 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.
